item.title: 2026.48.4 beta 1
item.description:
Mark-up holds through a reload, and a hidden sidebar still shows who's waiting

Wortel 2026.48.4 beta 1 · 2026-11-27

Mark-up holds through a reload. When an agent changed a file while you marked up its page, the dev server reloaded the page and your marks and note were gone. A page’s own reload, or a jump it makes by itself, now waits while you mark up and until the note is copied. The reload button in the tab’s header shows a dot while one waits, and the note bar says “The page changed. It loads when you copy.” It happens once you copy or press Esc. A link you click, and Back and Forward, still go through at once.

Your typing stays in the note. Clicking the session in the sidebar, picking the tab or ⌘] could hand the keyboard to the page during mark-up, so a space scrolled it and a page shortcut could act. The note keeps the keyboard now.

A long note scrolls. Past six lines the note bar cut its first and last lines in half and the caret went out of sight. It scrolls now, keeps the line you are typing in view, and a note you come back to opens where you left the caret.

A dot on the sidebar button. With the sidebar hidden (⌘B), nothing in the window said a session was waiting. The sidebar button in the title bar now carries the dot of the most urgent one, in its colour, and its tooltip says what kind it is.

Smaller things. A beta now names the release it leads up to: this is 2026.48.4 beta 1, and 2026.48.4 replaces it when it comes out, whether or not you still take betas. Send Feedback names the version as About does.

Split it anywhere, and mark up what you see

Wortel 2026.48.3 · 2026-11-27

Splits, each with its own tabs. ⌘D splits the split you are in to the right and ⇧⌘D splits it down, each with a new terminal. A tab let go on the edge of a split makes a new split there, and let go on its middle moves into it. Changes and Files still open beside the terminal with ⌥⌘B, and ⌘J still takes you to a terminal under the main one. ⇧⌘↩ zooms the split you are in to the whole window and back, and View ▸ Reset Layout puts every tab back where a session starts with it, closing nothing.

A tab that asks what it should be. The + in a split’s row, or ⌥⌘T, opens an empty tab listing Terminal, Browser, Changes, History and Files. Click one or press its first letter. ⌘] and ⌘[ walk the splits, ⌃⌥⌘ and an arrow goes to the split on that side, and ⌃⌘ and an arrow moves the tab in front there.

Mark up what you see. Mark Up (⇧⌘M) works over a page in a browser tab, a file’s source, its diff, rendered Markdown and an image. Click an element of a page, or draw around anything with a box, a pen, an arrow or a highlighter. Your note goes in a bar at the bottom, with each mark in it as a chip. Return copies it as plain text with a picture of each mark, ready to paste to an agent. Nothing is typed or sent for you.

The browser tab grew up. ⌘F finds in a page, with Safari’s keys. A download is saved to Downloads, named .download until it is whole. It never replaces a file and is never opened, and a button in the tab’s header lists what was saved. An .html file opens as the page it makes, reloads when the file changes, and ⌥⌘U shows its source.

Smaller things. wortel split opens a terminal in a split beside a session, and wortel split down -- <command> runs a dev server or a log there. A session made with wortel new is now filed right after the session that ran it. A slow start shows a spinner on its empty page. A beta now says “Wortel Beta” in the menu bar, the Dock and Finder, so you can tell it from the regular app. Settings ▸ Beta updates takes this Mac off the beta channel.

Usage data. Wortel now counts when mark-up is turned on and when a note is copied: over which kind of preview, roughly how many marks, and whether one was a picked element. It also counts wortel split, and a tab opened in a split. Never what was marked, a word of the note, or any file, folder or repository name.

Files on ⌘P, a preview tab, and links that open again

Wortel 2026.48.1 · 2026-11-25

Links open again. In 2026.47.4 a ⌘-clicked web link opened nothing, a middle click pasted nothing, and on macOS 15 a ⌘-clicked path outside a repository could hang Wortel. All three are fixed. Selected text is kept for a middle click and no longer replaces what you copied with ⌘C. A long path an agent broke over two rows now opens whole.

Files on ⌘P. Once you type, ⌘P lists the files in the session’s repository or folder. Return opens one in a tab, and name:120 opens it at that line.

A preview tab. A file you pick in Changes or Files shows in one tab with its title in italics, and the next one takes its place. Double-click to keep it. With the terminal in front a click only selects, so your agent stays in view, and Space opens the preview. The diff under the Changes list can be put away from View ▸ Show Diff in Changes.

New sessions open clean. A session that starts an agent used to show the prompt, the command typed on it, then the agent popping in. It now stays an empty page until the agent has drawn, two seconds at most. Keys typed meanwhile reach the agent once it’s up, except Return.

Help on a new Mac. When there is no agent or no git, the raised hand in the sidebar says so and types the official install line for you to run. A claude installed by its own installer is now found in every session. Wortel asks to send notifications the first time it has one, not at launch.

Claude Code redraws at any width. New sessions open Claude Code in its fullscreen view, which redraws the whole conversation when the terminal changes size, so a diff drawn while a column was open no longer stays narrow. A renderer you chose in Claude’s own settings is kept.

Safer with what’s in the terminal. A program can no longer read your clipboard. Git in Changes and History no longer runs a diff or signature program that a repository’s own config names.

Smaller things. Closing a session goes back to the one you were in before it, not the row above. exit closes its session again instead of showing a red banner. The font is SF Mono on every Mac: without Apple’s separate download it had been JetBrains Mono. An agent can end its own session and worktree with wortel close, and Wortel asks you about uncommitted files first. A folded section shows the working dots of a session inside it. A server Claude Code started no longer keeps its session working. ⌘↑ and ⌘↓ jump between prompts. Wortel’s source is open, under the GPL.

Usage data. After Wortel hung and was force quit, the next launch reports where it was stuck, for how long and roughly how much memory it held, as it does for a crash. It also counts an agent too old to report its state, and a file picked on ⌘P, never which. File, folder and repository names are still never collected.

Terminals kept whole while Wortel is closed, and agents that come back on their own

Wortel 2026.47.4 · 2026-11-20

This update restarts your shells once. Installing it ends every session’s shell and starts a new one, once, because the part of Wortel that keeps them running has changed. Claude Code, Codex and Pi come back by themselves, each in its own conversation, and your shell history is saved as usual. Anything else that was running, like a dev server, needs starting again. If Restart Now does nothing, quit Wortel with ⌘Q to finish the update.

Your terminals are kept whole. Wortel used to rebuild a terminal’s screen when it opened, and that could come back narrow, doubled or in pieces. The process that keeps your shells running now keeps each terminal as well, so after a quit, an update or even a crash a session is exactly as it was, scrollback included, with whatever an agent drew while Wortel was closed. A session out of sight for a minute gives its memory back and returns the same way when you open it.

Agents come back where they were. After a restart each agent resumes its own conversation, even when several share a folder. One you opened and never typed into starts fresh instead of joining someone else’s. An agent that starts while Wortel is closed now tells Wortel what it’s doing, like any other, and so does every agent this update restarts.

Fixes. Restart Now in the update dialog sometimes did nothing. Wortel now quits by itself a few seconds after you click it. Claude Code started through another command, like caffeinate -i claude, now resumes its conversation too.

More than one window, and terminals that come back as you left them

Wortel 2026.47.3 · 2026-11-20

More than one window. Window ▸ New Window (⇧⌘N) opens a second window with a sidebar of its own. Drag a session onto the other window’s sidebar to move it there, or out of the window to give it one of its own; it keeps running as it is. A session’s menu has Move to New Window and Move to Window, and Window ▸ Merge All Windows puts everything back in one. Closing a window closes its sessions, asking first if something is running in them. New Worktree Session is ⌥⇧⌘N now, since ⇧⌘N opens a window.

Your terminals come back as you left them. After you quit or update, a session’s terminal used to start empty and its agent printed what it could again, sometimes narrow or twice over. Every session’s screen and scrollback are now kept when Wortel quits and put back when it opens, before anything else. It starts with the first quit after this update; the update itself comes back the old way. After a crash, the shells are still there and the agent draws its screen again, as before.

Restart agents that were already running. Claude Code and Pi sessions already running when you update won’t show when they’re working until you restart them. They ask whether the terminal is listening only when they start.

Agents say what they’re doing. Claude Code, Codex, Pi, opencode and others now tell Wortel when they’re working, waiting for your approval, asking a question, finished or failed, and Wortel no longer guesses from the title or the screen. A Codex turn that ended no longer arrives as “needs input”.

Smoother, steadier terminals. Resizing the window or dragging the divider keeps up with the pointer. A terminal no longer ends up under the side column after you switch sessions, a session you come back to after a while is no longer drawn in scattered pieces, and agents out of sight work at the width you’ll see them at.

The sidebar sorts. Each section has Sort By in its ”…”: Recent Activity, Date Created, Name, or by hand. Folders come before loose sessions, section headers are easier to read, and pressing the session you’re in puts the keyboard back in its terminal.

Smaller things. ⌘-clicking a path an agent printed opens it in Wortel at its line. A new agent session that would start in your home folder gets a folder of its own in ~/Wortel, and sessions opened at home are called Home. Every terminal follows light and dark at once, and text stays readable when you switch. ⌘O and renaming a folder work again.

Usage data. Wortel now counts when a window is opened, with roughly how many are open, and when sessions move between windows, and how. It still never collects what you type, what your terminals show, or the names of your files, folders or repositories.
